findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - An existing client keeps an ignored, untracked Forge guide under `.agents` and upgrades Forge.
If the ignore rule is in an untracked `.agents/.gitignore`, `forge upgrade` accepts the checkout because it ignores untracked files (`src/forge/upgrade.py:82-85`) and creates a separate worktree from the committed branch (`src/forge/upgrade.py:176-178`). Neither the local guide nor its ignore rule is in that worktree, so sync creates the new guide without saving the original. After the upgrade merges, a normal pull can overwrite the ignored local guide: Git merge updates ignored files by default. Its contents are then absent from both Git and the backup.
Adds work: preserve ignored local guides across the upgrade worktree; F 1 x H 1 = 1; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Preserve existing .agents guides before replacing them

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - A team shares its Forge guide between hosts by making `.agents/skills/forge/SKILL.md` a symlink to `.codex/skills/forge/SKILL.md`, and the shared guide has uncommitted team edits. `story.ships` lists the Codex path before the agents path, so `sync.write` overwrites the shared file before this backup reads it. The reported `.pre-forge-` file consequently contains the new template, and the team edits are lost. Capture the agents pages before writing any host path.
findings.title: Preserve existing .agents guides before replacing them

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo initialized with this release upgrades to a later release that changes the Forge guide. Sync creates a `.pre-forge-*` copy of the previously generated `.agents` guide, and `forge upgrade` commits that untracked backup. `review_skip.upgrade_only` accepts only paths returned by `sync.synced`; the backup is not in the sync inventory, so an otherwise mechanical upgrade invokes the model reviewer. This can block an upgrade when the reviewer is unavailable, and the new-client cases in `tests/test_upgrade_skips_model_review.py` expect no review call. The named upgrade proof misses this because it upgrades to the already-installed template.
findings.title: Keep generated backups from forcing a model review on upgrades

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - An existing client ignores `.agents/` because it contains local agent files. During upgrade, sync writes the new guide in the upgrade worktree, but `close.synced_changes` uses `git status` without ignored files, so `upgrade.py` never stages it. The subsequent sync check uses the same status-based inventory and can pass; the upgrade commit and other checkouts receive no `.agents` guide. A new repository with that ignore rule also fails init because `repo.commit_state` explicitly adds the ignored paths without forcing them. This leaves the promised init and upgrade delivery incomplete.
findings.title: Not done: Deliver the .agents guide when its directory is ignored

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A review reaches its limit with both a blocking P0 and a blocking lower-priority finding. The guide says lower-priority findings stop the item and ask the owner, while the new sentence says the P0 returns to the worker. `close.py:412-413` instead postpones the owner stop whenever any P0 remains open. The same unconditional owner-stop claim appears at `skill.md:2580`, so the generated guide can direct a coordinator to ask for a choice that close has not requested. The updated guide test asserts the unconditional sentence and does not catch this contradiction.
findings.title: Not done: Explain the round limit when P0 and lower findings coexist

why: The generated copies of the Forge skill in client repos disagree on the review round rule (one copy asks the owner after the second blocked round even for new findings, another describes P0 continuation)
